body: Why some of these are not switched on

A legacy Hindi font is not an encoding. It is a font whose glyphs happen to sit on ASCII codepoints, and every vendor arranged them differently. Converting one correctly means knowing exactly which key carried which letter, and that has to come from real documents. It cannot be inferred.

So the pages above exist, with their titles and descriptions, but the ones marked Coming soon deliberately have no converter on them. A converter built on a guessed map produces Hindi that looks plausible and is quietly wrong in ways you would only find out later, which is worse than no converter at all.
“Hindi” and “Unicode” mean the same thing here

Text typed on an Android, iPhone or Windows Hindi keypad is already Unicode. So “Hindi to Kruti Dev” and “Unicode to Kruti Dev” are the same conversion and the same page, Unicode to Kruti Dev. Mangal is a Unicode font too, which is why Kruti Dev to Mangal really means “Kruti Dev to Unicode, shown in Mangal”.

body: What this converter does

Kruti Dev is not an encoding. It is a font whose glyphs happen to sit on ASCII codepoints, which is why a Kruti Dev document opened on a machine without the font shows up as gibberish like Hkkjr instead of भारत. Converting it to Unicode is not a matter of swapping one letter for another. The characters have to be reordered, because the two systems store Hindi differently.

This page does that reordering properly. Type or paste on the left and the Unicode output appears on the right as you type. There is no Convert button to hunt for, no advertisement between you and the text box, and no upload.
Why the output may look different from other converters
Two things go wrong in most Kruti Dev converters, and both are easy to miss because the broken output still looks like Hindi:

• The short-i matra. In Kruti Dev you type the ि before the consonant, because that is where it is drawn. Unicode wants it after. If a converter copies the visual order straight across, you get text that renders acceptably in some fonts but fails search, sorting, spell-check and screen readers.
  • The reph. The र् that rides above a letter is typed after its syllable in Kruti Dev, so कर्म is keyed as deZ. It has to be moved to the front of the cluster, and it has to be moved before the i-matra is repositioned, or words like कीर्ति come out scrambled.
Split vowel signs are handled too: Kruti Dev builds ो out of an aa-matra plus an e-matra, so dks has to be recomposed into को rather than left as two separate marks.
Who needs this

Government offices across India still run on Kruti Dev. Court orders, file notings, tender documents, school records and exam papers were typed in it for two decades. But portals, databases and e-governance systems all expect Unicode, so every time an old document has to go into a new system, somebody has to convert it. Typists preparing for CPCT, RSCIT and state stenography exams need the reverse direction just as often.

faq.q: Is this Kruti Dev to Unicode converter free?
faq.a: Yes, completely. There is no signup, no character limit and no paid tier. The converter is a static web page, so there is nothing to charge for.

faq.q: Does my text get uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. The entire conversion engine is JavaScript that runs inside your browser. Your text is never sent to a server, which means you can convert confidential file notings and draft orders without them leaving your machine. You can disconnect from the internet after the page loads and it will still work.

faq.q: Why does the i-matra (ि) come out in a different place than in my Kruti Dev file?
faq.a: Because that is correct. Kruti Dev stores glyphs in visual order, so the short-i sign is typed before its consonant. Unicode stores them in logical order, where the sign belongs after the consonant. So fd becomes कि, not ि followed by क. Converters that skip this step produce text that looks right but breaks search, sorting and spell-check.

faq.q: What about conjuncts like क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ and श्र?
faq.a: They are mapped explicitly, along with the reph (र्), the rakar (्र), half letters and nukta characters. The reph is the other common failure: in Kruti Dev it is typed after the syllable it sits on, so कर्म is keyed as deZ and has to be moved back into place.

faq.q: Will my English words and numbers be converted too?
faq.a: While the checkbox under the panels is ticked (it is by default), dates, numbers and percentages are left untouched and common English words are detected and kept. URLs and email addresses are never changed. Because a legacy font stores Hindi as plain ASCII, an unusual proper noun can still be converted by mistake. Untick the checkbox to convert everything. Numbers come out the same either way: Kruti Dev 010 draws its number keys as English digits, and its Hindi digits, typed with Alt codes, are always converted.

body: “Hindi to Kruti Dev” is this page

If you type Hindi on an Android or iPhone keypad, or with the Windows Hindi keyboard, or paste it from WhatsApp or a website, that text is already Unicode. There is no separate “Hindi” format to convert from. So this one page covers both “Hindi to Kruti Dev” and “Unicode to Kruti Dev”. They are the same conversion.
The same goes for Mangal and Nirmala UI: both are Unicode fonts, so text in either of them can be pasted straight into the box on the left.
Unicode to Kruti Dev, the right way round

Converting into a legacy font is harder than converting out of one, because the text has to be put back into visual order. Every short-i matra has to move to the front of its consonant cluster, every reph has to move to the end of the syllable it belongs to, and the composed vowel signs ो, ौ and ॉ have to be split back into the two glyphs Kruti Dev draws them with.
This page does all of that as you type. The output is plain ASCII, which is what Kruti Dev text is, and it turns into Hindi the moment the Kruti Dev font is applied to it.
What to do with the output

1. Copy the right-hand panel, or use Download .docx.
  2. Paste into Word, LibreOffice or your DTP application.
  3. Select the pasted text and set the font to Kruti Dev 010. The .docx download does this step for you.
Who uses this direction

Printing presses and DTP shops that have twenty years of Kruti Dev templates. Candidates for court, district and state clerical typing tests whose notification asks for Kruti Dev, and who need practice passages in that font. Offices that receive a Unicode draft from one department and have to fit it into a legacy template from another. And anyone maintaining an old publication where switching the whole archive to Unicode is not realistic.
A note on exact spellings

Kruti Dev often offers more than one way to key the same letter. Where that happens the converter picks a single canonical spelling, so its output may not be byte-identical to text a person typed by hand. It renders identically, and converting it back with the Kruti Dev to Unicode converter returns exactly what you started with.

faq.q: I want to convert Hindi to Kruti Dev. Is this the right page?
faq.a: Yes. Hindi typed on a phone keypad, the Windows Hindi keyboard, or copied from a website or WhatsApp is already Unicode. "Hindi" and "Unicode" mean the same thing here, so "Hindi to Kruti Dev" and "Unicode to Kruti Dev" are one page. Paste it into the left box and you will get Kruti Dev on the right.

faq.q: Can I type Hindi directly into the box instead of pasting?
faq.a: Yes. Switch your keyboard to Hindi and type into the left box, which is set up for Devanagari input. To type Hindi phonetically in English letters ("namaste" for नमस्ते), use English to Hindi typing, then paste the result here.

faq.q: Why would I convert Unicode back to Kruti Dev?
faq.a: There are three common reasons. First, a printing press or DTP operator still works in Kruti Dev and needs the file in that font. Second, a typing test or stenography exam is conducted in Kruti Dev and you want practice material. Third, an old template has to stay consistent with documents typed years ago.

faq.q: Will the result be identical to text originally typed in Kruti Dev?
faq.a: It will be equivalent, but not always character-for-character identical. Several Kruti Dev key sequences produce the same letter (क can be keyed two different ways), so the converter picks one canonical spelling. Converting back to Unicode returns the original text either way.

faq.q: What happens to English words and numbers?
faq.a: English digits are never changed, so an amount keeps its value, and Kruti Dev 010 shows them as English digits too. Hindi digits such as २०२४ are written with the Alt-code characters Kruti Dev 010 draws them on, so they still show as २०२४. English words, URLs and email addresses stay as typed. With the checkbox under the panels ticked (the default), dates stay exactly as typed too, for text shown in an English font. If everything will be in Kruti Dev, untick it, and the / in a date is typed with the Kruti Dev key that draws it.

body: First, the thing nobody tells you

Mangal is a font, not an encoding. It is the Unicode Devanagari font that Microsoft has shipped with Windows since XP. Kruti Dev, by contrast, is a legacy font that maps Hindi onto ASCII slots, which is why a Kruti Dev document looks like Hkkjr on a computer that does not have it.

So "Kruti Dev to Mangal" is really "Kruti Dev to Unicode, shown in Mangal". The text this page gives you is standard Unicode Hindi. Paste it into a form, a portal, an email or a database and it will be correct regardless of which Devanagari font ends up rendering it.
Why your department asks for Mangal

When Unicode Hindi first became practical in government work, Mangal was the only Devanagari font you could rely on being installed on every Windows machine. Specifying it in a circular was a way of guaranteeing that a form would look the same in every office. That instruction has outlived its reason, because Nirmala UI and Noto Sans Devanagari render the same text just as well, but the wording survives in departmental guidance, which is why people search for "Kruti Dev to Mangal" rather than "to Unicode".

If a portal rejects your text, the problem is almost never the font. It is usually that the text was pasted as Kruti Dev ASCII rather than converted, or that the matra order is wrong, which is precisely what this converter fixes.
Getting it into a document as Mangal

1. Paste your Kruti Dev text on the left. The Mangal output appears as you type.
  2. Press Download .docx for a Word file with Mangal already applied, or Copy text to paste it yourself.
  3. If you paste manually into Word, select the text and pick Mangal from the font list. Setting the font does not change the characters, it only changes how they are drawn.

Is the whole file in Kruti Dev? Use the Upload Word file tab above the boxes instead. You get the .docx back with its Hindi in Mangal, and its tables and formatting as they were.
Mangal, Nirmala UI or Noto?

Mangal is the oldest and has the most conservative letterforms, which is why it still reads as the "official" choice. Nirmala UI, introduced with Windows 8, is cleaner on screen. Noto Sans Devanagari is Google's open font and is what this site uses for its own Hindi text. All three display identical Unicode, so pick whichever your form asks for, and do not worry that the underlying text changes. It does not.
Need plain Unicode without the Mangal framing? Use the Kruti Dev to Unicode converter. Going the other way? Try Mangal to Kruti Dev.

faq.q: Is Mangal a different encoding from Unicode?
faq.a: No, and this is the single most useful thing to know here. Mangal is a font, not an encoding. It is an OpenType Unicode font that Microsoft ships with Windows. So "Kruti Dev to Mangal" means "Kruti Dev to Unicode, then displayed in Mangal". The text this page produces is ordinary Unicode Hindi and will work in any Unicode font.

faq.q: Why do government forms specifically ask for Mangal?
faq.a: Because Mangal was the first Devanagari font guaranteed to be present on every Windows machine, so specifying it meant a form would render the same way in every office. Many departmental circulars still name it by habit. In practice any Unicode Devanagari font (Mangal, Nirmala UI, Noto Sans Devanagari) displays the same characters.

faq.q: The output panel does not look like Mangal on my device.
faq.a: The panel asks for Mangal first and falls back to another Devanagari font if it is not installed, which is normal on Mac, Linux, Android and iOS, where Mangal does not ship. The characters are identical either way. On Windows it renders in genuine Mangal once Mangal is installed. On Windows 10 and 11 it comes in the optional Devanagari Supplemental Fonts pack, which you can add under Optional features in Settings.

faq.q: How do I get the converted text into a Word file as Mangal?
faq.a: Use the Download .docx button. The file is written with Mangal already applied to every paragraph. Or copy the text, paste it into Word, select it and choose Mangal from the font list.

faq.q: Is the matra order handled correctly?
faq.a: Yes. The short-i sign is moved after its consonant, the reph is moved to the front of its cluster, split vowel signs are recomposed and the conjuncts क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ and श्र are mapped explicitly. This is the part most converters get wrong, and it is why text from elsewhere sometimes fails search or spell-check even though it looks fine.

faq.q: Can I go the other way?
faq.a: Yes. See the Mangal to Kruti Dev converter. There is a link to it under the boxes on this page too.

body: Mangal to Kruti Dev in one step

Mangal is a Unicode font, so "Mangal text" is just Unicode Hindi: the same text you would get from a website, a modern Word document or a WhatsApp message. Kruti Dev is a legacy font that stores Hindi as ASCII in visual order. Going from one to the other means undoing every reordering rule that Unicode applies.

That is what this page does as you type: short-i signs move back in front of their consonants, rephs move to the end of their syllables, composed vowel signs like ो split back into their two drawn parts, and half letters are re-encoded to the separate glyphs Kruti Dev uses for them.
Reading the output

The right-hand panel will look like nonsense English, something along the lines of Hkkjr. That is correct and expected. Kruti Dev text only becomes Hindi when the Kruti Dev font is applied to it. Two ways to get there:

• Download .docx. The Word file comes out with Kruti Dev already applied to every paragraph.
  • Copy Kruti code, paste into your document, select it, and set the font to Kruti Dev 010.

For a whole Mangal document, use the Upload Word file tab above the boxes. The .docx comes back with Kruti Dev 010 on the Hindi, while English, tables and formatting stay as they were.
Typing tests and legacy templates

The most common reason people need this direction is exam practice. Several court, district and state clerical typing tests still set Hindi typing in Kruti Dev, while practice passages are almost always published as Unicode. Converting them here gives you material in the font those exams use. CPCT is different: it offers InScript or a Unicode version of the Remington layout, so check its own key chart.

The other common reason is production work. A press with twenty years of Kruti Dev layouts cannot re-set them all in Unicode, so incoming Unicode copy has to be converted to fit the existing template.
Round-tripping

Kruti Dev frequently offers more than one key sequence for the same letter, so the output here uses one canonical spelling rather than reproducing exactly what a human typist would have pressed. It renders identically, and running it back through the Kruti Dev to Unicode converter returns the text you started with. If you want the forward direction with Mangal framing, use Kruti Dev to Mangal.

faq.q: What counts as "Mangal" text for this converter?
faq.a: Any Unicode Hindi. Mangal is a font rather than an encoding, so text displayed in Mangal, Nirmala UI, Noto Sans Devanagari, Aparajita or Kokila is all the same underlying Unicode. Paste from a Word file, a website, a PDF or WhatsApp. It all works.

faq.q: The output is English letters, not Hindi. What went wrong?
faq.a: Nothing. Kruti Dev text is ASCII, and it only becomes Hindi once the Kruti Dev font is applied. Use the Download .docx button, which sets the font for you, or paste into Word and choose Kruti Dev 010 from the font list.

faq.q: Why would anyone convert Unicode back to a legacy font?
faq.a: Typing tests and stenography exams in several states are still conducted in Kruti Dev, so candidates need practice passages in it. Printing presses and DTP operators often have decades of Kruti Dev templates. And offices regularly receive a Unicode draft that has to be dropped into an old legacy-font layout.

faq.q: Will my numbers and dates survive?
faq.a: Yes. English digits are kept as they are, so an account number or an order date keeps its value, and Kruti Dev 010 shows them as English digits. Hindi digits such as २०२४ are written with the Alt-code characters Kruti Dev 010 draws them on, so they still read २०२४. Words in English, web addresses and email addresses are not touched. By default the checkbox under the panels is ticked, and dates are then left character for character, which suits text that stays in an English font. For a page that will be all Kruti Dev, clear the checkbox: the / in a date is then typed with the Kruti Dev key that draws it.

faq.q: Does it handle conjuncts and the reph?
faq.a: Yes. The i-matra is moved back to the front of its cluster, the reph is moved to the end of its syllable, composed vowel signs are split back into the two glyphs Kruti Dev draws them with, and क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ, श्र plus the nukta letters are all mapped.

faq.q: Do I need Mangal installed?
faq.a: No. You need a Devanagari font to read the input panel, and almost every modern device has one. You do not need Mangal specifically, and you do not need it installed for the conversion itself.

/english-to-hindi-typing.h1: English to Hindi Typing (Roman to Hindi)
/english-to-hindi-typing.title: English to Hindi Typing, Free Online
/english-to-hindi-typing.description: Free English to Hindi typing tool. Type Hindi in Roman letters - namaste becomes नमस्ते - and get Unicode Hindi or Kruti Dev instantly. Works offline too.
/english-to-hindi-typing.lede: Type Hindi using the English keyboard you already have. Write it the way it sounds and the Devanagari appears as you type - no Hindi keypad, no install, no sign-up.
body: Type Hindi without a Hindi keyboard

Most people who need to write a line of Hindi do not have a Hindi keyboard set up, and do not want to install one for a single WhatsApp message or form field. This page solves that: you type namaste and get नमस्ते, you type mera naam ram hai and get मेरा नाम राम है. The English letters are read as sounds and written back out in Devanagari.

The output is ordinary Unicode Hindi, so it works everywhere - WhatsApp, email, Word, government portals, social media, search. If you need the legacy Kruti Dev font instead, paste the result into the Unicode to Kruti Dev converter.
Transliteration is not translation

This is the one thing worth being clear about before you use it. The page changes the script, not the language. Type computer and you get कंप्यूटर - the English word written in Devanagari - not the Hindi word for a computer. That is almost always what people want when they are typing a message, because the sentence they have in their head is already Hindi. They just cannot type the letters.
Spelling rules worth knowing
You do not need to learn a system. Type the word as it sounds and it will usually be right. These few patterns cover the letters English has no spelling for:

• Aspirated consonants add an h. kh ख, gh घ, ch च, chh छ, th थ, dh ध, ph फ, bh भ, sh श.
  • Long vowels double. aa आ, ee or ii ई, oo or uu ऊ. So kitab and kitaab both give किताब, but doubling is the way to be sure.
  • Conjuncts have short spellings. ksh क्ष, tra त्र, gya ज्ञ, shr श्र, and ri for ऋ.
  • Nasals look after themselves. An n or m before another consonant becomes the anusvara, so hindi gives हिंदी and mandir gives मंदिर.

faq.q: Does it translate English into Hindi?
faq.a: No, and the difference matters. This is transliteration, not translation: it writes the sound of what you typed in Devanagari. Type computer and you get कंप्यूटर, not संगणक. If you want the meaning changed rather than the script, you need a translator.

faq.q: What is the Exact (ITRANS) mode for?
faq.a: It turns the guessing off. ITRANS is a precise notation where aa ii uu are the long vowels, capitals T D N S are the retroflex consonants, and .n is the anusvara. Nothing is inferred, so the output is always exactly what you wrote - raaShTriiya gives राष्ट्रीय every time. Useful for names, Sanskrit and anything that has to be right the first time.

faq.q: A word came out wrong. Can I pick a different spelling?
faq.a: Yes. Tap or click the word in the Hindi box and up to five spellings appear under it. Pick one and only that word changes. You can also edit the Hindi box directly.

faq.q: What happens to punctuation and numbers?
faq.a: They stay exactly as you typed them - chal? becomes चल? and 10 baje becomes 10 बजे. The one exception is |, which becomes the Hindi full stop । (and || becomes ॥). To keep an English word in English, wrap it in backticks: `Google`.

faq.q: How do I type the letters English has no spelling for?
faq.a: Aspirated consonants take an h: kh ख, gh घ, th थ, dh ध, bh भ, ch च, chh छ, sh श. Long vowels double: aa आ, ee ई, oo ऊ. For ऋ write ri, and for क्ष त्र ज्ञ write ksh tra gya.

faq.q: Does my text get uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: In Hinglish mode, yes - what you type is sent to Google's public input-tools service, which is what decides that thela is ठेला and not थेला. Web addresses and email addresses are removed before anything is sent. In Exact (ITRANS) mode nothing you type leaves your browser. If you go offline, or Google cannot be reached, the page falls back to its built-in dictionary automatically and keeps working - you will just see a note saying the spelling is coming from there.

problems.fix: Switch Typing to Exact (ITRANS). Every sound then has one fixed spelling, so the result is exactly what you typed.

/hindi-typing-test.h1: Hindi Typing Test - Kruti Dev Remington Typing Tutor (Free)
/hindi-typing-test.title: Hindi Typing Test: Kruti Dev, CPCT, SSC
/hindi-typing-test.description: Free Hindi typing tutor and test on the Kruti Dev Remington layout: 11 lessons, finger guide and 1-minute to 2-hour tests with live WPM. For CPCT, SSC, court.
/hindi-typing-test.lede: Learn Hindi typing on the Kruti Dev Remington layout that many Hindi typing exams use. An on-screen keyboard shows the next key, the hand guide shows which finger presses it, and eleven lessons take you from the home row to full paragraphs. Practice tests run from 1 minute to 2 hours, you can pause the clock, and you can submit at any point to see your result. Free, unlimited, and nothing is uploaded.
body: A tutor, not just a test

Most Hindi typing pages hand you a paragraph and a clock. That measures where you are, but it does not move you. This one teaches the layout: the key you need next is lit on the keyboard, the finger that should press it is coloured on the hands, and the passage marks every akshara green or red as you go. When a letter needs Shift, it also shows which little finger should be holding it.

The passage is ordinary Unicode Hindi, so it renders on any machine with nothing installed. What the tutor checks underneath is the Kruti Dev keystrokes that produce it, worked out by the same conversion engine that powers the converters on this site - so what you read and what you press are guaranteed to be the same sentence.
The lessons

Eleven levels. The first five each open one more row. Level 1 is the home row alone - क, स, र, ह, य and four matras, all typed without moving a finger off its resting key. Then the top row, the bottom row, numbers, and Shift.

Once every key is reachable the levels stop being about rows and start being about the script. Level 6 is the matras - ि ी ु ू े ै ो ौ - on consonants you already know, so the only new thing on screen is the vowel sign and the rule that ि is typed before its letter. Level 7 drills the letters with no key of their own - भ, श, ष, ण, ध, ख, घ, झ, थ - which are two keystrokes each and are where most Kruti Dev typists quietly lose their speed. Level 8 is the four conjuncts क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ and श्र, which look like new letters and are not: they are built from letters you have, with the halant you already use. Levels 9 to 11 are everyday words, sentences and finally paragraphs.
A level unlocks the next when you type the whole drill at its accuracy target. Speed is recorded but never required, because gating on speed teaches you to rush a drill you have not learned yet.

faq.q: Is this Hindi typing tutor free?
faq.a: Yes. No signup, no limit on attempts, no paid tier. It is a static page that runs in your browser, so there is nothing to charge for and nothing to log in to.

faq.q: How long are the tests?
faq.a: Practice tests run for 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes, 1 hour or 2 hours, and there is enough queued text that you cannot run out even at 60 words per minute. The long options are there because departmental and court typing papers run far past the ten minutes a speed test needs, and stamina is a separate skill from speed - a typist who is comfortable for one minute is often finished by minute eight. A test that long does reuse paragraphs, since the passage pool is finite. Lessons have no clock at all: the timer counts up and the drill ends when you have typed it.

faq.q: How is WPM calculated?
faq.a: Five keystrokes count as one word, which is the convention every typing test uses and the only fair way to compare a Devanagari passage with a Latin one. The headline number is net WPM - correct keystrokes only. The result card also shows gross WPM, which counts every keystroke whether it was right or not. Exams score net.

faq.q: Is my typing sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. The passage, the clock, your score and your lesson progress all stay in this browser tab. Nothing you type is uploaded, there is no account, and no result is recorded anywhere we can see. Progress is kept in your own browser storage on this device and goes away if you clear your browsing data.

problems.fix: Check that Windows is set to the English keyboard, not a Hindi one: the tutor reads English keys and checks them against the Remington keystrokes. Then check Caps Lock.

problems.fix: Capitals are the Shift layer, so Caps Lock changes every letter. Turn it off and hold Shift with the little finger of the other hand instead.

/hindi-keyboard.h1: Hindi Keyboard Online - Type in Hindi Without a Hindi Keypad
/hindi-keyboard.title: Hindi Keyboard Online, Type Hindi Free
/hindi-keyboard.description: Free on-screen Hindi keyboard. Tap Devanagari letters to write Hindi without installing a keypad - vowels become matras by themselves - then copy it.
/hindi-keyboard.lede: Click the Devanagari letters to write Hindi - no keypad to install and no layout to learn. Copy the Unicode when you are done. Nothing is uploaded.
body: Type Hindi on any computer

Most people who need a line of Hindi do not have a Hindi keypad set up and are not about to install one for a single form field, a WhatsApp message or a name that has to be written correctly. That is what this page is for. The letters are on screen, you click them, and the Hindi builds up in the box above. When you are finished you copy it and paste it wherever it was going.

The output is ordinary Unicode Devanagari, which is what every modern system expects - government portals, email, Word, search, social media, databases. If you specifically need the legacy font instead, paste it into the Unicode to Kruti Dev converter.
How the letters are arranged

In वर्णमाला order, the order every Hindi speaker learned at school: the vowels, then the consonants in their five groups (with the halant, anusvara, chandrabindu and visarga beside them), then the everyday conjuncts, then digits. Space, Backspace, Enter and the full stop । are on the bottom row.

This is deliberately not an InScript picture. InScript scatters Devanagari across the QWERTY key positions, which is exactly right if you have learned the layout and are looking for the physical key - and exactly wrong if you are finding each letter by eye, because the letters end up in no order at all. Anyone who does know InScript has it installed already and can simply type. This page is for everyone else.
Matras, half letters and conjuncts
Three things cover almost everything people get stuck on:

• Vowels turn into matras after a consonant. Click क, then इ, and you get कि - even though the sign is drawn to the left of the letter. The vowel keys show the matra they will type, so there is no separate matra row to hunt through.
  • The halant makes a half letter. ◌् after a consonant silences its vowel, so क + ् + य is क्य. That is how every conjunct is built.
  • The common conjuncts have their own keys. क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ and श्र turn up constantly, so they are one click rather than three.

The dotted circles on the sign keys are not characters. A vowel sign has no shape of its own, so the circle stands in for the consonant it will attach to - the same convention the Unicode charts use. Only the sign itself is inserted.
Second layer

More letters opens the rest: the Sanskrit vowels (ॠ ऌ ॡ), the candra signs English loanwords use (ऑ in डॉक्टर), the Marathi and southern letters, the nukta, and the remaining punctuation. None of it is needed for ordinary Hindi, which is why it is behind a toggle rather than on the first screen.
Getting Kruti Dev out of it

Copy the text and paste it into the Unicode to Kruti Dev converter. It gives you the legacy keystrokes to paste into Word with Kruti Dev 010 applied, and it tells you if any character has no Kruti Dev equivalent.
Where this fits with the rest of the site

If you would rather spell Hindi words out in English letters than hunt for each character, English to Hindi typing is faster for whole sentences - type namaste and get नमस्ते. If you want to build real typing speed, the Hindi typing test measures it. And if you already have a document in the wrong font, you want a converter: Kruti Dev to Unicode, Unicode to Kruti Dev, or the full list.

faq.q: How do I type in Hindi without a Hindi keyboard?
faq.a: Click the letters on this page. They are laid out in वर्णमाला order - vowels first, then the consonant groups - so you find a letter by reading rather than hunting. What you click appears in the box above, and you copy it out when you are done. Nothing has to be installed.

faq.q: Is this Hindi keyboard free?
faq.a: Yes, completely. No signup, no limit, no paid tier. It is a static page that runs entirely in your browser.

faq.q: How do I type a matra like ि or ी?
faq.a: Tap the consonant, then the vowel. After a consonant the vowel keys turn into matras by themselves - they show ◌ि ◌ी ◌ा so you can see what you will get - so क then इ gives कि, and क then आ gives का. At the start of a word the same keys type the full vowel. The dotted circle only shows where the sign attaches. It is never inserted.

faq.q: How do I type a half letter or a conjunct?
faq.a: Use the halant - the ◌् key at the end of the consonants. A consonant, then halant, then another consonant joins them: क + ् + य gives क्य. The four conjuncts Hindi uses constantly - क्ष त्र ज्ञ श्र - have their own keys so you do not have to build them each time.

faq.q: Can I still use my own keyboard?
faq.a: Yes, and you should for anything you can already type. Nothing on this page blocks the physical keyboard: numbers, punctuation, space, backspace, arrow keys, selection, paste and undo all behave normally. Click the letters you cannot type and type the rest.

faq.q: Can I get Kruti Dev instead of Unicode?
faq.a: This page writes Unicode Hindi. Copy it and paste it into the Unicode to Kruti Dev converter, which gives you the Kruti Dev code for MS Word.

faq.q: Does it work on a phone?
faq.a: Yes. On a phone or tablet the keys dock to the bottom of the screen like a phone keyboard, and the text box stays at the top, so you can see both while you type. Your phone's own keyboard stays closed while the Hindi keys are open. Press Use my keyboard to switch back to it.

faq.q: Is my text uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Everything runs inside your browser, and what you type is never sent to a server. Once the page has loaded you can disconnect from the internet and it keeps working.

/all-converters.title: All Hindi Tools | Font Converters, Typing, Amount in Words, Dates
/all-converters.description: Every tool on MyKrutiDev in one place: Kruti Dev, DevLys, Mangal, Chanakya and Preeti converters, amount in words, Hindi dates, typing tests and more.

/devlys-to-unicode.title: DevLys to Unicode Converter | DevLys 010 to Hindi Unicode Online
/devlys-to-unicode.description: Convert DevLys 010 Hindi text to Unicode with correct matras and conjuncts. Free and browser-based, with nothing uploaded.
/devlys-to-unicode.lede: Paste DevLys 010 text on the left and get Unicode Hindi on the right, with matra order and conjuncts handled properly. Nothing is uploaded.
body: What this converter does

DevLys is not an encoding. It is a font whose glyphs sit on ASCII codepoints, which is why a DevLys document opened on a machine without the font shows gibberish like Hkkjr instead of भारत. Turning it into Unicode is not a matter of swapping one letter for another - the characters have to be reordered, because the two systems store Hindi differently.
Paste on the left and the Unicode appears on the right as you type. No Convert button to hunt for, no advertisement between you and the text box, and no upload.
DevLys and Kruti Dev: close, and checked

DevLys 010 and Kruti Dev 010 share a keyboard layout. That is genuinely useful - it means two decades of Hindi DTP work is interchangeable at the keystroke level - but it is also the assumption that quietly breaks most converters, because the two fonts are not identical everywhere.

So it was verified rather than assumed. Every character code this converter uses was read out of both font files and compared: advance width, contour count and bounding box. All of them match. The two fonts do diverge in one block of character codes, and the conversion table deliberately does not use any code in that block. That is why this page is live and why the Chanakya pages are not.
What usually goes wrong elsewhere

• The short-i matra. In DevLys you type the ि before its consonant, because that is where it is drawn. Unicode wants it after. Copy the visual order straight across and you get text that renders acceptably in some fonts but fails search, sorting, spell-check and screen readers.
  • The reph. The र् that rides above a letter is typed after its syllable, so कर्म is keyed as deZ. It has to be moved to the front of the cluster, and moved before the i-matra is repositioned, or words like कीर्ति come out scrambled.
  • Split vowel signs. DevLys builds ो from an aa-matra plus an e-matra, so dks has to be recomposed into को rather than left as two marks.
Who needs this

DevLys turns up wherever Hindi DTP was done in the 1990s and 2000s: press and publishing files, school and college records, tender documents, old court and municipal paperwork. Modern portals, databases and e-governance systems all expect Unicode, so every time one of those files has to go into a new system, somebody has to convert it.

For the other direction use Unicode to DevLys, and DevLys to Mangal shows the result in the Mangal font most government forms ask for. If your document is actually Kruti Dev, Kruti Dev to Unicode is the page you want.

faq.q: Is the DevLys to Unicode converter free?
faq.a: Yes. No signup, no character limit, no paid tier. The page is static and the conversion runs in your browser, so there is nothing to charge for.

faq.q: Is DevLys 010 the same as Kruti Dev 010?
faq.a: They are different fonts that share a keyboard layout. Every key this converter uses draws the same Hindi letter in both - that was checked by comparing the two font files glyph by glyph, not assumed. So a DevLys document and a Kruti Dev document containing the same keystrokes hold the same Hindi, even though the letterforms on screen differ slightly.

faq.q: Then why was this page "coming soon" for so long?
faq.a: Because "almost the same" is not good enough for a converter. The two fonts genuinely do differ in one block of character codes. The page went live only once it was confirmed that the conversion table never touches that block, so the overlap it relies on is real rather than approximate.

faq.q: Does my text get uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. The whole engine is JavaScript running inside your browser. Your text is never sent to a server, so confidential notings and draft orders never leave your machine. Once the page has loaded you can disconnect from the internet and it still works.

faq.q: Why is the short-i matra (ि) in a different place than in my DevLys file?
faq.a: Because that is correct. DevLys stores glyphs in visual order, so the short-i sign is typed before its consonant. Unicode stores them in logical order, where the sign belongs after. So fd becomes कि. Converters that skip this step produce text that looks right but breaks search, sorting and spell-check.

faq.q: What happens to English words, numbers and dates?
faq.a: By default the checkbox under the panels is ticked, and then numbers, dates and percentages pass through unchanged while common English words are recognised and kept. Web and email addresses are never touched, ticked or not. A legacy font keeps Hindi as plain ASCII, so a rare proper noun can still be turned into Hindi by mistake. Clear the checkbox to convert the whole text.

faq.q: Can I convert Unicode back into DevLys?
faq.a: Yes. Each page converts in one fixed direction, so use the Unicode to DevLys converter for the reverse. There is a link under the boxes too. That page also accepts Hindi typed on a phone or the Windows keypad, since keypad Hindi is already Unicode.

/unicode-to-devlys.title: Unicode to DevLys Converter | Hindi Unicode to DevLys 010 Font
/unicode-to-devlys.description: Convert Unicode Hindi back to DevLys 010 font text online. Live conversion, correct half-letters, no upload, free.
/unicode-to-devlys.lede: Type or paste Unicode Hindi on the left and get DevLys 010 font text on the right, ready to paste into Word. Nothing is uploaded.
body: What this converter does

This is the direction you need when a document has to go back into a legacy workflow: a press file, a school register, a form that was laid out in DevLys years ago and still has to match. You type Hindi the modern way - phone keypad, Windows Hindi keyboard, or pasted from anywhere on the web - and get DevLys keystrokes out.

The output will look like nonsense Latin text, and that is correct. DevLys stores Hindi as ASCII and relies on the font to draw the letters. Paste it into Word, select it, apply DevLys 010, and it reads as Hindi.
The reordering, in reverse

  • Unicode to Kruti Dev: Hindi you typed on a keypad back into Kruti Dev keys, for a form or template that still demands the legacy font.
  • Kruti Dev to Mangal: the same Unicode output, labelled for people whose documents are set in Mangal.
  • Mangal to Kruti Dev: the reverse.
  • All converters: the full list, including the ones still being verified.
Hindi, Unicode and Mangal are the same thing

Text typed on a phone or on the Windows Hindi keypad is already Unicode. The characters are real Devanagari: न is stored as the letter न, and any font can draw it. Mangal is simply one such font, shipped with Windows. So "Hindi", "Unicode" and "Mangal" describe one kind of text with three names, and this site labels the boxes "Unicode / Hindi" so both audiences recognise their own word.
That is also why there is no separate "Hindi to Mangal" page. There would be nothing for it to do.
Kruti Dev and DevLys are not Hindi

A legacy font works the other way round. Kruti Dev does not store Devanagari at all. It stores ordinary English letters and punctuation, and the font file draws a Hindi glyph in place of each one. The word नमो is stored as the four characters ueksS.
Two consequences follow, and between them they explain almost every problem people bring to a converter:

• Without the font, the text is unreadable. Send a Kruti Dev document to someone who does not have Kruti Dev installed and they see the raw keystrokes. Paste it into a website and it stays gibberish forever, because a web page cannot borrow a font from your hard disk.
  • Nothing can search or spell-check it. To a computer it is English nonsense. Search, sorting, screen readers and translation all fail.
Converting to Unicode fixes both permanently. That is the direction worth taking if you have a choice.
Working out which font an old document used

Open the file and look at the font name in the toolbar. That is usually the fastest answer. If the file has lost its formatting, the keystrokes themselves are a clue: Kruti Dev and DevLys 010 share almost the same layout, so fgUnh reading as हिन्दी points at one of those two. Chanakya and Shusha use genuinely different layouts and will not decode correctly with a Kruti Dev map, which is why their pages stay marked coming soon rather than returning plausible-looking rubbish.
If the text already looks like Hindi on a machine with no special fonts installed, it is Unicode and needs no conversion at all.

faq.q: Which Hindi font converter do I actually need?
faq.a: Work backwards from where the text is going. Going into a website, WhatsApp, email or a government portal, you need Unicode, so use Kruti Dev to Unicode. Going into an old Word template or a form that must stay in Kruti Dev, you need the legacy keys, so use Unicode to Kruti Dev.

faq.q: Is Hindi the same as Unicode?
faq.a: For this site, yes. Anything typed on a phone or on the Windows Hindi keypad is already Unicode Hindi. The two words describe the same text, which is why the boxes are labelled "Unicode / Hindi". Kruti Dev and DevLys are the exception: they are not Hindi at all, they are English keystrokes that a font draws as Hindi.

faq.q: Why does my Kruti Dev text look like gibberish?
faq.a: Because it is. A Kruti Dev document stores ueksS, not नमो. The Hindi only appears when the Kruti Dev font is installed and applied. Open the same file on a machine without the font and you see the raw keystrokes. That is normal, and it is exactly what this converter translates.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mangal and Unicode?
faq.a: None, at the level that matters. Mangal is a Unicode font: a Mangal document already contains real Devanagari characters. Converting "Kruti Dev to Mangal" and "Kruti Dev to Unicode" produces the same characters. The only difference is which font your document is set to display them in.

faq.q: Do Kruti Dev and DevLys use the same keyboard?
faq.a: Yes, for every key the converters use. DevLys 010 and Kruti Dev 010 are different fonts that share the Remington layout, and the two font files were compared glyph by glyph before the DevLys converters went live. The letterforms on screen differ slightly, but the same keystrokes hold the same Hindi.

faq.q: Is my text uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every converter on this site runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you paste is sent to a server, logged or stored. You can disconnect from the internet after the page loads and it still works.

Hindi numbers are not built from parts the way English ones are. Every number from 1 to 99 is its own word, so 39 is उनतालीस and 79 is उनासी, and that is exactly where people slip when they write an amount by hand. This tool has all hundred of them written out, in the spellings used in school books and bank forms.
Above a hundred the Indian place values take over: सौ, हज़ार, लाख, करोड़, अरब and खरब. So 98,76,54,321 is अट्ठानवे करोड़ छिहत्तर लाख चौवन हज़ार तीन सौ इक्कीस.

IAST and ISO 15919 give each Devanagari letter one Roman spelling, with marks for what English letters cannot show: long vowels (ā ī ū), retroflex letters (ṭ ḍ ṇ ṣ) and the nasal marks. Every a is written

Both standards write the vowel a after every consonant that carries one, so भारत is bhārata, not "bharat". Hindi drops some of those a sounds in speech, but which ones cannot be told from the spelling, so a tool that dropped them would be guessing. Here nothing is guessed.
IAST or ISO 15919?
They agree on most letters. ISO 15919 also marks the long ē and ō and writes ऋ as r̥, which keeps ड़ (ṛ) apart. IAST writes ऋ as ṛ, so in IAST mode this tool writes ड़ as r̤.

faq.a: With the ISO 15919 letters, in both modes: ज़ is z, फ़ is f, क़ is q and ऑ is ô.

faq.a: No. The tool runs in your browser and nothing you type leaves your computer.

Hindi ए and ओ are long, so they become ఏ and ఓ. The dot in ज़ or फ़ is dropped, giving జ and ఫ, because few Telugu fonts draw one.
A Telugu reader says the a at the end of every word, so भारत written in Telugu is read bhārata. For Roman letters instead, use Hindi to IAST.

faq.q: Will a Telugu speaker understand the result?
faq.a: They will be able to read it aloud. Understanding it depends on whether they know Hindi, because the words are still Hindi words.

faq.q: What happens to English words and numbers?
faq.a: They stay as they are. Hindi digits such as १२३ are changed into the digits of the new script.

faq.q: Is anything I type uploaded?
faq.a: No. The tool runs in your browser and nothing you type leaves your computer.

/about.title: About MyKrutiDev | Who Builds These Hindi Font Tools and How
/about.description: Who runs MyKrutiDev, how the Kruti Dev converters and typing tutor are built and tested, and why your text never leaves your browser.
/about.lede: MyKrutiDev is a small, independent site that converts Hindi between legacy fonts and Unicode and teaches Hindi typing - accurately, for free, and without uploading anything.
body: What we make

We make converters between Kruti Dev, DevLys, Mangal and Unicode, a Hindi typing tutor with timed tests on the Remington layout, an on-screen Hindi keyboard, English to Hindi typing, printable charts and guides to the problems people bring us. Everything is free and needs no account.
How we check it

Hindi conversion goes wrong in small, costly ways: the short-i matra on the wrong side of its consonant, a reph on the wrong syllable, a conjunct split in two. So every rule in the converters is tested against real documents and against the fonts themselves. The Kruti Dev keyboard chart is read out of the Kruti Dev 010 font file, key by key, and more than a thousand automated tests run before any change goes live. A font pair that has not been verified is marked as coming soon rather than guessed at.
Your text stays on your computer

The converters and the typing tutor run entirely in your browser. What you paste or type is not uploaded, logged or stored by us. The one feature that uses an outside service is English to Hindi typing in Hinglish mode, which asks Google's input service how to spell each word. The privacy policy sets out exactly what that means.
Who we are

The MyKrutiDev team is a small group of developers and Hindi typists who have spent years moving office documents between Kruti Dev and Unicode. We are not affiliated with the makers of Kruti Dev, DevLys, Chanakya or Mangal, or with any exam body. To report a wrong conversion or suggest a feature, contact us.

/hindi-typing-finger-chart.h1: Hindi Typing Finger Chart - Free PDF
/hindi-typing-finger-chart.title: Hindi Typing Finger Chart PDF | Which Finger for Which Key (Remington)
/hindi-typing-finger-chart.description: Free printable finger chart for Remington (Kruti Dev) Hindi typing: every key marked with the finger that presses it, readable in black and white.
/hindi-typing-finger-chart.lede: Which finger presses which key on the Remington (Kruti Dev) layout. Each key carries a short finger code, so the chart reads just as well printed in black and white.
body: Why fingers matter

Speed in a typing test comes from never looking down, and that only works if every key always belongs to the same finger. Beginners who type with two fingers plateau early. Learners preparing for SSC, CPCT or court typing tests should fix the finger for each key before chasing speed.
The typing tutor shows the same assignment live, lighting up the finger for each key as you type.

faq.q: Which finger presses Shift?
faq.a: The little finger of the other hand. For a letter typed with the left hand, hold Shift with the right little finger, and the other way round - holding Shift with the same hand is the most common beginner mistake.

faq.q: Why do the index fingers have so many keys?
faq.a: Each index finger covers two columns, so it owns eight keys, not four. Those are also the easiest reaches, which is why many common Hindi letters sit there.

/hindi-typing-practice-sheets.h1: Hindi Typing Practice Sheets - Free PDF
/hindi-typing-practice-sheets.title: Hindi Typing Practice Sheet PDF | 11 Kruti Dev Lessons (Free)
/hindi-typing-practice-sheets.description: Free Hindi typing practice sheets PDF: one A4 sheet per lesson, home row to paragraphs, each line with the Kruti Dev keys to press. Remington layout.
/hindi-typing-practice-sheets.lede: Eleven A4 sheets, one for every lesson in the typing tutor - from the home row to full paragraphs. Every line shows the keys to press on the Remington (Kruti Dev) layout.
body: Who these sheets are for

Beginners who want to practise away from the screen, teachers running a typing class, and learners preparing for SSC, CPCT, court and state typing tests. The lines are the tutor's own drills, and the keys under each line are exactly the keystrokes the tutor checks.
How to use them

Work through the sheets in order, because each lesson only uses keys the earlier ones taught. Type each line on paper-in-front, eyes-on-sheet, then check your speed and accuracy in the online tutor and write it in the progress log.

faq.q: How long does it take to learn Hindi typing?
faq.a: With 20-30 minutes a day, most learners know the whole keyboard in two to three weeks and reach 25-30 words per minute in about two months. Daily practice matters more than long sessions.

faq.q: Why are the keys printed under every line?
faq.a: Remington typing is learned by the keys, not the letters: भ is two keys, and ि is typed before its consonant. Seeing the sequence while you type builds the right habit from the first day.

faq.q: Are these the same lessons as the online tutor?
faq.a: Yes - the sheets are printed from the tutor's lesson data, so sheet 4 is lesson 4, line for line.

/kruti-dev-matra-chart.h1: Kruti Dev Matra and Conjunct Chart - Free PDF
/kruti-dev-matra-chart.title: Kruti Dev Matra Chart PDF | How to Type ि ी र् क्ष त्र ज्ञ श्र (Free)
/kruti-dev-matra-chart.description: Free Kruti Dev matra and conjunct chart PDF: the exact keys for ि ी ु ू े ै ो ौ, ्र, reph, क्ष त्र ज्ञ श्र and nukta on the Remington layout.
/kruti-dev-matra-chart.lede: The key sequence for every matra, the two ways of writing र (्र below, reph above), the four joined conjuncts क्ष त्र ज्ञ श्र, and the nukta - on one A4 page.
body: The two rules that trip everyone up

The i-matra ि is typed before its consonant, and the reph (the र that sits on top) is typed after the whole syllable. Everything else goes in the order you read it. Beginners and exam candidates (SSC, CPCT, court) lose more marks to these two than to anything else.
Practise them in lessons 6-8 of the typing tutor, or convert a finished text with Unicode to Kruti Dev to see the keys for any word.

faq.q: Why is the i-matra typed first?
faq.a: Remington follows the typewriter, which printed what you see from left to right - and ि is drawn to the left of its consonant. Unicode stores it after, which is why converters have to reorder it.

faq.q: How do I type a half letter?
faq.a: Most consonants have a half form on their own key, usually the Shift layer. For the joined conjuncts क्ष त्र ज्ञ श्र the chart gives the exact keys.

/kruti-dev-alphabet-chart.h1: Kruti Dev Alphabet Chart (Hindi Varnamala) - Free PDF
/kruti-dev-alphabet-chart.title: Kruti Dev Alphabet Chart PDF | Keys for Every Hindi Letter (Free)
/kruti-dev-alphabet-chart.description: Free Kruti Dev typing chart PDF: the keys for every Hindi vowel, consonant, half letter and digit on the Remington layout, from अ to ह, on one A4 page.
/kruti-dev-alphabet-chart.lede: Every vowel, every consonant with its half form, the Hindi digits and the danda, with the exact Kruti Dev 010 keys or Alt codes to press - on one A4 page to keep beside the keyboard.
body: How to read the chart

Under each letter are the keys to press, left to right. Shift + means hold Shift while you press the key. Many letters take two keys: आ is अ followed by the aa-matra, and the letters with a standing bar (ख घ झ ण थ ध भ श ष) are their half form followed by the bar, the k key.

The half forms make conjuncts: type the half letter, then the full one (क् + य = क्य). For the matras, the reph and the joined letters क्ष त्र ज्ञ श्र, use the matra and conjunct chart. To learn the keys by heart, start lesson 1 of the typing tutor.

faq.q: How do I type ऊ in Kruti Dev?
faq.a: ऊ has no key of its own. With Num Lock on, hold Alt and type 0197 on the number pad: Kruti Dev 010 draws ऊ for that character. On a laptop without a number pad, write the text in Unicode and convert it with Unicode to Kruti Dev.

faq.q: How do I type ङ and ञ?
faq.a: Neither has a key. With Num Lock on, hold Alt and type 0179 on the number pad for ङ, or 0165 for ञ: Kruti Dev 010 draws them on those characters. Hindi often writes the anusvara in their place: गंगा rather than गङ्गा, and चंचल rather than चञ्चल.

faq.q: Do the number keys type Hindi digits?
faq.a: No. In Kruti Dev 010 the number keys 1 to 9 and 0 type English digits. The Hindi digits have Alt codes: Alt+0131 is १, Alt+0132 is २ and so on up to Alt+0139 for ९, and Alt+0229 is ०. Shift + a types the danda ।.

/kruti-dev-alt-codes.h1: Kruti Dev 010 Alt Code Chart - Free PDF
/kruti-dev-alt-codes.title: Kruti Dev Alt Codes PDF | Hindi Digits, ऊ, ङ, ञ, द्द, ट्ट (Free)
/kruti-dev-alt-codes.description: Free Kruti Dev 010 Alt code chart: the Alt codes for the Hindi digits ० to ९, ऊ, ङ, ञ, ँ and ready-made conjuncts like द्द, ट्ट, ह्न and क्त, on one A4 page.
/kruti-dev-alt-codes.lede: The characters no Kruti Dev 010 key types - the Hindi digits, ऊ, ङ, ञ, ँ and the ready-made conjuncts - each with the Alt code that types it in Word on Windows.
body: How to type an Alt code

Set the text in Kruti Dev 010 and turn on Num Lock. Hold the Alt key, type the four digits on the number pad (not the number row above the letters), then let go of Alt. Word puts in a character such as ƒ, and Kruti Dev 010 draws it as १.

On a laptop without a number pad, type the text in Hindi and convert it with Unicode to Kruti Dev, which writes these characters for you. The ready-made conjuncts can also be typed from the keyboard with half letters: द्द is n~n. Every code on the chart was checked against the Kruti Dev 010 font file, and Kruti Dev 011, 012, 014 and 016 draw the same letters.

faq.q: Why do I see ƒ instead of १?
faq.a: The text is not set in Kruti Dev. ƒ is the character Windows types for Alt+0131: select the text, choose Kruti Dev 010 as the font, and the same character is drawn as १.

faq.q: Do these codes work in every Kruti Dev font?
faq.a: In Kruti Dev 010, 011, 012, 014 and 016, yes. Kruti Dev 055 and 020 put other letters on several of these codes, and their number keys already type Hindi digits.

/hindi-typing-progress-log.h1: Hindi Typing Progress Log - Free PDF
/hindi-typing-progress-log.title: Hindi Typing Progress Log PDF | Track WPM and Accuracy (Free)
/hindi-typing-progress-log.description: Free printable Hindi typing progress log: 30 rows for date, lesson, WPM, accuracy and notes. Track your practice for SSC, CPCT and court typing tests.
/hindi-typing-progress-log.lede: A one-page log with 30 rows: date, lesson or test, WPM, accuracy and the keys to work on. Filling it in takes ten seconds and shows you exactly where your speed comes from.
body: Why keep a log

Progress in typing is slow enough that you cannot feel it day to day. A written record makes the plateau visible - and shows whether you are pushing speed before accuracy. Candidates for SSC, CPCT and court typing tests should log every timed test.
Take the numbers from the online tutor, which shows WPM and accuracy after every lesson and test.

faq.q: What speed do I need for a typing test?
faq.a: It depends on the exam: many Hindi typing tests ask for 20 to 30 words per minute, with a limit on mistakes. Check your notification, and log your accuracy as well as your speed.

faq.q: How often should I test myself?
faq.a: Once a day is plenty. Practise lessons for most of your session and finish with one timed test, then write the result here.

/kruti-dev-010-font.h1: Kruti Dev 010 Font: Install It, Check It, Read It Without It
/kruti-dev-010-font.title: Kruti Dev 010 Font | Install on Windows and Check It Works
/kruti-dev-010-font.description: What the Kruti Dev 010 Hindi font is, how to install it on Windows and Mac, how to check it works, and how to read Kruti Dev text with no font installed.
/kruti-dev-010-font.lede: Kruti Dev 010 is the Hindi typewriter font many government offices, courts and typing exams still use. If a file shows English letters like Hkkjr instead of Hindi, paste them below and read them now - then install the font so the file shows properly in Word.

steps: Paste the text that looks like Hkkjr into the Kruti Dev box. The Hindi appears in the other box at once, with no font installed.
Check names and figures against the paper copy or the PDF, if you have one - they are the words where a mistake would matter.
Copy the Unicode to use it anywhere, or install the font (steps below) and keep working in Kruti Dev.
howTo.tip: To check whether the font is installed, type Hkkjr in Word and pick Kruti Dev 010 from the font list. If it turns into भारत, it works.

problems.problem: Kruti Dev 010 is not in Word's font list
problems.fix: Word reads its font list when it starts. Close every Word window and open it again. If it is still missing, the install did not finish: right-click the .ttf and choose Install for all users.

problems.problem: The file shows English letters on another computer
problems.fix: The font lives on your computer, not inside the .docx. The other machine needs Kruti Dev 010 as well - or send a PDF, or convert the text to Unicode so it reads anywhere.

problems.problem: A few letters come out wrong
problems.fix: You probably have another member of the family (011, 016, 055) rather than 010. They share most keys but not all. Install Kruti Dev 010 itself.

problems.problem: It will not work on a phone or in Google Docs
problems.fix: Neither lets you add a font, so Kruti Dev shows as English letters there. Convert to Unicode on this page. Unicode Hindi displays on every phone.

faq.q: Is Kruti Dev 010 a Unicode font?
faq.a: No. It is a legacy font: it draws Hindi letters on the codes of English keys. The file stores Hkkjr and only the font turns it into भारत, which is why the text breaks the moment the font is missing.

faq.q: Can I download Kruti Dev 010 from this site?
faq.a: No. We do not hand out font files whose licence we cannot confirm. Your office IT section, your typing institute or a reputable font library are the usual sources. You do not need the font to use this site: the converters work without it.

faq.q: How is Kruti Dev 010 different from 011, 016 or 055?
faq.a: They are different designs in the same family. Most keys are shared, but some characters sit on different keys, so text typed in one can come out slightly wrong in another. Exams and most offices specify 010, and the converters here are built and tested for 010.

faq.q: Should new documents be in Kruti Dev 010 or Unicode?
faq.a: Unicode, unless an exam, a court or an office template requires Kruti Dev. Unicode opens correctly everywhere and can be searched. The Kruti Dev vs Unicode guide goes through the trade-offs.

body: What Kruti Dev 010 is

Kruti Dev 010 is a Hindi font from before Unicode. Instead of storing Devanagari letters, it reuses the codes of the English keyboard: press d and the file stores the letter d, but the font draws क. Its layout is the Remington typewriter keyboard, which is why typists, offices, courts and typing exams across the Hindi-speaking states still ask for it.

The catch is that the Hindi exists only while the font is present. Open the same file where Kruti Dev 010 is not installed and you see the raw keys - Hkkjr instead of भारत. The text is not damaged. It is being drawn by a font that treats it as English.
How to install it on Windows

1. Get the font file, usually Kruti_Dev_010.ttf or K010.TTF, from a source you trust. If it came as a .zip, extract it first - Windows cannot install a font from inside a zip.
  2. Right-click the .ttf and choose Install for all users, or Install if you do not have administrator rights.
  3. Close Word completely, open it again, and pick Kruti Dev 010 from the font list.
On a Mac, double-click the file and choose Install Font in Font Book. The installation guide covers the errors people run into most.
Reading Kruti Dev without installing anything

To read, check or reuse a Kruti Dev document you do not need the font. The converter at the top of this page turns Kruti Dev into Unicode Hindi in your browser and moves the ि sign and the reph to where Unicode expects them. For a whole Word file, use Kruti Dev to Unicode, which converts .docx files and keeps the layout.

/hindi-typing-test-for-exams.navSub: SSC, CPCT and court exam practice
/hindi-typing-test-for-exams.h1: Hindi Typing Test for SSC, CPCT and Court Exams
/hindi-typing-test-for-exams.title: Hindi Typing Test for CPCT, SSC, LDC Exams
/hindi-typing-test-for-exams.description: Practise the Hindi typing skill test for SSC, CPCT, High Court and district court exams in Kruti Dev (Remington), timed, with net WPM and accuracy.
/hindi-typing-test-for-exams.lede: Practise the Hindi typing skill test the way it is set: Kruti Dev on the Remington layout, a timed passage, and a result in net words per minute with accuracy. Choose the length your exam uses and sit it in full.

steps: Choose Practice test and the length of your exam - 10 min for an SSC CHSL-style test, 15 or 30 min to build stamina.
Type the passage without looking down. Wrong keys turn red. Correct them only if your exam allows backspace.
Read Net WPM and accuracy on the result, and write them in the progress log to compare week by week.
howTo.tip: Exams score speed and accuracy together. A clean 28 WPM usually beats a careless 35, so get accuracy above 95% first.

problems.problem: My speed collapses in a full-length test
problems.fix: That is stamina, not skill: short tests flatter everyone. In the last three weeks, sit at least one full-length test a day. Pause and resume rather than abandoning a run.

problems.problem: I keep mistyping ि
problems.fix: In Kruti Dev the ि sign is typed before its consonant: fd for कि. Repeat lesson 6 until it is automatic - it is the commonest error in exam passages.

problems.problem: The exam keyboard layout was not the one I practised
problems.fix: Remington and InScript are different keyboards. The notification names the layout or the font (Kruti Dev means Remington and Mangal usually means InScript). Practise only that one.

problems.problem: Conjuncts and half letters slow me down
problems.fix: क्ष, त्र, श्र and the half letters have their own keys or key pairs. The matra and conjunct chart lists each with its exact keys.

faq.q: Which font and layout does the Hindi typing test use?
faq.a: The notification and the exam-day instructions say. SSC's CHSL 2021 instructions listed InScript, Kruti Dev, Remington (GAIL) and Remington (CBI) for Hindi. CPCT types in Unicode on Remington (GAIL) or InScript. Court and state exams often name Kruti Dev 010. If you learned on a typewriter or at a typing institute, you learned Remington.

faq.q: Is backspace allowed in the exam?
faq.a: It depends on the exam. Some allow corrections and score what is left. Others disable backspace or count every error. Practise both: correct as you go in some tests, and in others do not correct anything.

faq.q: How many words per minute do I need?
faq.a: For most Hindi typing posts the bar is between 20 and 30 WPM at a set accuracy. Aim about 5 WPM above your target so that a nervous day still passes.

faq.q: Are these real exam passages?
faq.a: No. The passages are general Hindi prose written for practice, not copies of any exam paper. They use the same letters, matras and conjuncts, so they build the same skill.

body: Which exams test Hindi typing

Hindi typing is a qualifying skill test in many recruitments: the SSC CHSL typing test for LDC and JSA posts, CPCT in Madhya Pradesh, High Court and district court exams for typists and clerks, and state clerical exams such as the Rajasthan LDC (Clerk Grade II). The rules change from one notification to the next, so treat the figures below as typical and check yours for the final word.

• SSC CHSL (LDC, JSA): 10 minutes on a computer. Hindi needs 30 words per minute, which SSC defines as 9,000 key depressions an hour at five key depressions a word. The test only qualifies: it adds no marks. SSC's skill-test instructions for CHSL 2021 listed InScript, Kruti Dev, Remington (GAIL) and Remington (CBI) as the Hindi layouts, so check the list in your notice. Candidates eligible for a scribe get compensatory time under SSC's rules.
  • CPCT (Madhya Pradesh): Section B has an English and a Hindi typing test of 15 minutes each, typed in Unicode on Remington (GAIL) or InScript. The scorecard reports speed and accuracy for each. To qualify you need 20 net WPM in Hindi and 30 in English, and a post can ask for more.
  • High Court, district courts and state clerk posts: the speed, the font and the error limit are set by each notification. Many still use Kruti Dev 010 on the Remington layout.
Passage length, time and errors

At 30 WPM a 10-minute test is 1,500 key depressions: 300 words of five keystrokes. Errors are counted against the passage. Most notifications count an omitted, wrong or extra word as a full mistake, and spacing, punctuation or capitalisation as a half mistake. The share of errors allowed differs by post and category, and the exact weights are in your notification. Get errors under 5% first, then push the speed.
How your speed is counted

Exams count key depressions: every keystroke counts, and five keystrokes make one word. In Kruti Dev one Hindi letter can take two or three keys - भ is Hk, क्ष is {k - so 30 WPM in Hindi means fewer Hindi words than it sounds. The test on this page counts the same way, and its headline figure is net WPM: correct keystrokes only.
Practise the way the test is taken

Use the same layout as your exam, sit the full length, and keep your eyes on the passage rather than your hands. Warm up with the printable practice sheets, and if you are still learning the keys, start with the lessons in the Hindi typing tutor. The speed tips guide has a four-week plan, and Remington vs InScript explains the two layouts. Remington (GAIL) and Remington (CBI) are typewriter-style layouts too, but they do not match Kruti Dev key for key, so if your exam uses one of them, practise in that layout's demo as well.
Figures checked in October 2026 against SSC's published skill-test instructions and CPCT exam guides.

steps: Click the Kruti Dev box and type with the Remington layout: d for क, k for the ा sign, Hkkjr for भारत.
The other box shows your words as Unicode Hindi as you type, with the ि sign and the reph already where Unicode needs them.
Copy the Unicode into WhatsApp, email, Word or a form. It shows in any Hindi font, so the person reading it needs no Kruti Dev.
howTo.tip: Looking for a letter? Find it in the chart below: the top of each key is its Shift character, the bottom is what it types on its own.

problems.problem: The box I type in shows English letters
problems.fix: That is expected. Remington keystrokes are English letters until a font or a converter draws them as Hindi. The Unicode box beside it is your Hindi.

problems.problem: ि lands on the wrong letter
problems.fix: In Remington you type ि first: fd gives कि. Typed the other way round, df, it attaches to the next letter instead.

problems.problem: I cannot find half letters
problems.fix: They are mostly on Shift: D is क्, E is म्. Hold Shift with the little finger of the other hand, as on a typewriter.

problems.problem: Typing on a phone is awkward
problems.fix: Remington is a ten-finger layout for a physical keyboard. On a phone, the on-screen Hindi keyboard or your phone's own Hindi keypad is quicker.

faq.q: What is the Remington Hindi keyboard?
faq.a: The Hindi typewriter layout, brought to computers by fonts such as Kruti Dev and DevLys. Each Hindi letter sits on an English key - d is क, j is र - and letters without a key of their own are made from two, like Hk for भ.

faq.q: Is Remington the same as InScript?
faq.a: No. InScript is the Unicode layout built into Windows and Android, and it puts letters on different keys: on InScript k is क, on Remington it is the ा sign. Remington vs InScript compares them.

faq.q: Do I need Kruti Dev installed to type here?
faq.a: No. Your keystrokes are converted to Unicode Hindi in the browser, so the result shows in any font. You need Kruti Dev only if you want the raw keys to look like Hindi inside Word.

faq.q: Can I print the layout?
faq.a: Yes. The Kruti Dev keyboard chart is a one-page A4 PDF of this layout, and the finger chart shows which finger presses each key.

body: How the Remington layout works

Remington is the Hindi typewriter keyboard. Typists learned it on machines, and Kruti Dev 010 and DevLys carried it onto computers unchanged, which is why typing institutes and many exams still teach it. The most-used letters sit under the strongest fingers: the home row types ं े क ि ह ी र ा स य, so a typist resting there reaches a large share of everyday Hindi without moving.

Three habits cover most of the rest. Letters with no key of their own are built from a half form and the ा stroke: H is भ्, so Hk is भ. Shift gives most half letters. And the ि sign is typed before its consonant, because that is where it is drawn.
Typing Hindi here without learning it first

With the chart open you can hunt for keys, and the converter does the hard part: it turns Remington keystrokes into correctly ordered Unicode, putting ि after its consonant and the reph before its syllable. That is why the result can go straight into email or a website, where Kruti Dev text would show as English letters.
Learning it properly

For a typing exam, hunting for keys will not get you to 30 WPM. The Hindi typing tutor teaches this layout row by row with a finger guide, and the exam typing test times you the way SSC, CPCT and the courts do.

/how-to-type-hindi-in-ms-word.h1: How to Type Hindi in MS Word
/how-to-type-hindi-in-ms-word.title: How to Type Hindi in MS Word | 3 Easy Ways, Unicode or Kruti Dev
/how-to-type-hindi-in-ms-word.description: Three ways to type Hindi in Microsoft Word: English letters and paste, the Windows Hindi keyboard, or Kruti Dev - plus the Word settings Hindi needs.
/how-to-type-hindi-in-ms-word.lede: There are three ways to get Hindi into Word, and the right one depends on how much you type. The quickest needs nothing installed: type Hindi in English letters below, then copy it into Word.

steps: Type Hindi as it sounds, in English letters, in the box below: namaste becomes नमस्ते.
Copy the Hindi and paste it into your Word document. If the Hindi turns into boxes, pick Mangal or Nirmala UI for it.
Save the file as usual. The Hindi is Unicode, so it opens correctly on any computer or phone with no extra font.
howTo.tip: Paste with Keep Text Only (from the small clipboard icon Word shows after pasting) so the Hindi takes your document's font and size.

problems.problem: The Hindi becomes boxes when I change the font
problems.fix: The font has no Devanagari letters - Arial, Calibri and Times New Roman do not. Choose a Hindi font: Mangal, Nirmala UI, Kokila, Aparajita and Utsaah all come with Windows.

problems.problem: Changing the font does nothing to the Hindi
problems.fix: Word keeps a separate font for Hindi and other "complex scripts". Select the text, press Ctrl+D and set the font under Complex scripts.

problems.problem: Every Hindi word has a red underline
problems.fix: Word is checking Hindi against an English dictionary. Select the text, open Review → Language → Set Proofing Language and choose Hindi.

problems.problem: My office file is in Kruti Dev
problems.fix: Kruti Dev and Unicode cannot share a paragraph. Convert your Hindi with Unicode to Kruti Dev, paste it, and set the font to Kruti Dev 010.

faq.q: What is the best Hindi font for MS Word?
faq.a: For everyday documents, Nirmala UI (clean on screen) or Mangal (the traditional official choice), and Kokila reads well in print. All are Unicode fonts from Microsoft. Nirmala UI is always installed. Mangal and Kokila come in the Devanagari Supplemental Fonts pack, which you can add under Optional features in Settings if Word does not list them. Use Kruti Dev 010 only when a form or an office requires it.

faq.q: How do I switch on the Hindi keyboard in Windows?
faq.a: Open Settings → Time & language → Language & region, choose Add a language and add Hindi. Switch between English and Hindi with Windows key + Space. The standard Hindi keyboard is InScript, and Windows also offers a phonetic one in the language options.

faq.q: Can I type Hindi in Word on a Mac?
faq.a: Yes. In System Settings → Keyboard → Text Input → Input Sources, add Hindi: Devanagari (InScript) or Hindi - Transliteration, then switch from the input menu in the menu bar.

faq.q: Will this Hindi work in Google Docs and email?
faq.a: Yes. It is Unicode, the same as Hindi typed on a phone, so it shows anywhere that has a Hindi font - which is every modern phone and computer.

body: Three ways, from quickest to fastest
1. Type in English letters, paste into Word

The box above turns English spelling into Hindi: bharat becomes भारत. Nothing to install and nothing to learn, which makes it right for a letter, a form or a few paragraphs. For long documents a real keyboard layout is faster.
2. The Windows Hindi keyboard

Windows includes Hindi keyboards. Add Hindi as a language in Settings, then press Windows key + Space to switch while Word is open. InScript is the standard layout. The phonetic keyboard works like typing in English letters. Either way the result is Unicode, as in option 1.
3. Kruti Dev and the Remington layout

If you trained on a typewriter or for a typing exam, you may already know Remington. Install Kruti Dev 010, choose it in Word and type. It is fast for trained typists, but the result is legacy text that shows as English letters wherever the font is missing, so keep a Unicode copy of anything you send out.
Making Word behave with Hindi

• Set Hindi as the proofing language so Word stops underlining every word. With Hindi proofing tools installed it will spell-check Hindi too.
  • Use the Complex scripts font (Ctrl+D) to set the Hindi font for a whole document or style at once.
  • Give matras room. Signs like ि and ु reach above and below the line. If they touch the next line, use line spacing of 1.15 or more instead of "Exactly".
Moving between Kruti Dev and Unicode

Office files often mix both. Convert rather than retype: Kruti Dev to Unicode for old documents, Unicode to Kruti Dev when a template needs Kruti Dev. Both convert whole .docx files and keep tables and formatting.
