/privacy-policy.title: Privacy Policy: Files Stay on Your Device
/privacy-policy.description: MyKrutiDev converts text and files in your browser, so nothing you paste or upload is sent to us. What is stored on your device, and what Analytics counts.
/privacy-policy.lede: Short version: the converters and the typing tutor work inside your browser, so your text and your files never leave your computer. There are no accounts and no advertising. Google Analytics counts visits, and never sees your text or files.
body: Your text and your files

When you paste text into a converter, type in the tutor or drop in a Word or text file, all the work happens in JavaScript on your own device. The file is read by your browser, converted in memory and handed back to you as a download. It is never uploaded to MyKrutiDev or anyone else, and nothing on the site could receive it: the only things our server accepts are the short feedback form, the tool request form on the ToolMitra links page and, if you buy a PDF, the store order form, and only when you press Send or Pay. You can load a page, disconnect from the internet and keep converting.
The one exception: English to Hindi typing

On English to Hindi typing, the Hinglish mode sends each word you type to Google's public input-tools service to get its best Hindi spelling. Only the words being transliterated are sent, not the rest of the page, and web and email addresses are never sent. If you do not want that, switch Typing to Exact (ITRANS), which works entirely offline. Google's handling of those requests is covered by Google's own privacy policy.
What is stored on your device

• Your theme and colour choice, and your language choice.
  • In the converters: the text in the input box, so it is still there after a refresh, and the last 10 texts you converted with each tool, under Recent (each up to 50,000 characters). Clearing the box removes its draft, and Delete all empties Recent.
  • In the typing tutor: which lessons you have cleared, your best speed, your daily practice streak, badges, and your last 30 practice sessions.
  • A few interface preferences, such as whether key sounds are on.
  • The date you last sent feedback, so the feedback form does not ask again for 30 days.

These are kept in your browser's local storage, are never sent to us, and can be removed at any time by clearing this site's data in your browser settings. On a shared or office computer, use Delete all under Recent when you finish. The only cookies are Google Analytics' own, described below.

Your browser also keeps a copy of the site's own pages, scripts and fonts, so the converters open without an internet connection. That copy holds only the site's files, never your text.
Visit statistics (Google Analytics)

To learn which pages and tools people use, and what to improve, mykrutidev.com uses Google Analytics. For each visit it records the pages you open, how far you scroll, clicks on links to other sites and on downloads, the site or search that brought you here, your device type, browser, screen size and language, and your approximate location (city or country), which Google works out from your IP address. Google Analytics does not store the IP address itself. It also counts which buttons in the tools are used, such as Copy, Download Word, Print or a finished lesson, with the fonts or the lesson involved. It counts the start of a typing test (its mode and length) and that a file was chosen for conversion (its type and rough size, never its name or contents).

It sets two cookies, _ga and _ga_VZZRXNT8TQ, so that a returning visitor is not counted as a new one. They last up to two years. It never receives the text you convert, your files or anything you type in the tools, because those never leave your device. We have switched off Google signals and ad personalisation, so this data is not used for advertising, and the reports do not tell us who you are.

To opt out, block cookies for this site in your browser settings, use a tracker blocker, or install Google's Analytics opt-out add-on. The site works the same either way. Google's handling of this data is covered by Google's privacy policy.
Feedback
The Feedback button at the bottom of each page opens a short form, and only when you click it. If you press Send, we store:

• your rating (😞 😐 🙂 😍) and the options you ticked
  • what you wrote in the form's own text boxes, and an email address only if you chose to give one
  • the page you were on, the site language, the colour theme, whether you were on a phone or a computer, your screen width in pixels, your browser's name (for example "Chrome") and the date

We do not store your IP address, your browser's full identification string, or anything you typed, pasted or converted in the tools. Feedback is used only to decide what to fix and build next, and is kept in a Cloudflare D1 database that only the site's owner can read. A copy of each submission, with the email address if one was given, is also emailed to the site's owner through Resend, an email delivery service, so it can be answered quickly. An email address is used only to reply to you. It is never shared with anyone else or used for marketing. To have your feedback deleted, write to {email} from the address you gave.
Tool requests

The ToolMitra links page has a short form for suggesting the next tool. If you press Send, we store what you wrote in it, an email address only if you chose to give one, the site language, whether you were on a phone or a computer, and the date. Nothing else. Requests are kept in the same database as feedback, under the same rules: no IP address, read only by the site's owner, and an email used only to tell you when the tool is ready. A copy of each request is also emailed to the site's owner through Resend, in the same way. To have a request deleted, write to {email} from the address you gave.
Spam protection

To keep robots out, the feedback form and the tool request form use Cloudflare Turnstile, an invisible check that runs only after you open or start filling in a form (Cloudflare's own privacy policy covers it). To limit each visitor to 5 messages an hour on each form, the server keeps a one-way code made from your IP address and the current hour. The IP address itself is never saved, and the code is deleted once the hour is over.
Buying a PDF

If you buy a PDF, we ask for your email address and nothing else. We keep it with your order (what you bought, the amount and the Razorpay payment reference) so we can send the download link, let you download again and handle a refund. We do not use it for marketing and we never sell or share it.

You pay on Razorpay's own page. Razorpay handles your UPI, card or bank details under its own privacy policy, and we never see or store them. The order form uses the same invisible Cloudflare Turnstile check described above, and the download link is sent by email through Resend, an email delivery service.

Orders that are never paid are deleted after {unpaidDays} days. Paid orders are kept for as long as refunds and our accounts require, which can be several years. To ask about your order, write to {email}.
Server logs

The site is a set of static files served by a hosting provider. Like any web server, it may keep standard access logs - IP address, the page requested, browser type and time - for security and to keep the service running. These logs never contain the text or files you convert, because those never reach the server.
Children

The site asks no one for personal information, children included. The only places you can give any are the optional email boxes in the feedback form and the tool request form, and the email box when you buy a PDF. Buying is meant for adults, so children should ask a parent.
Changes and contact

install-kruti-dev-010-font-windows.h1: How to Install Kruti Dev 010 on Windows (and Check It Works)
install-kruti-dev-010-font-windows.title: Install Kruti Dev 010 Font on Windows
install-kruti-dev-010-font-windows.description: Install the Kruti Dev 010 Hindi font on Windows 10 or 11, check that Word can use it, and fix the problems that stop it showing up.
install-kruti-dev-010-font-windows.lede: Installing a font takes a minute. The trouble usually comes after: Word not listing it, text still showing English letters, or a different Kruti Dev turning up. This guide covers the install and all three.
body: Before you start

You need the font file for Kruti Dev 010, usually named Kruti_Dev_010.ttf, KRDEV010.TTF or K010.TTF. MyKrutiDev does not distribute it, because we cannot confirm its licence terms, so ask your office IT section or your typing institute for it, or get it from a reputable font library. Be wary of "font packs" that come as an .exe - a font is a .ttf or .otf file and never needs a program to install it.

Make sure it is the right one. The file name or its preview window should say Kruti Dev 010 - not 011, 016, 055 or a "Condensed" version. The family shares most keys but not all, and a near miss is behind many "a few letters come out wrong" complaints.
{{diagram:install-steps}}
Install it

1. Unzip it first. Right-click the .zip and choose Extract All. Windows lets you open a zip like a folder, but it will not install a font from inside one.
  2. Install for all users. Right-click the .ttf and choose Install for all users. On Windows 11 it may be under Show more options. Without administrator rights, choose Install and the font will work for your account only.
  3. Or drag it in. Open Settings → Personalisation → Fonts and drop the file on the "Drag and drop to install" area. It does the same thing.
  4. Restart the programs that need it. Word, Excel, PageMaker and CorelDRAW read the font list when they start, so close every window of them and open them again.
Check that it works

Open Word, choose Kruti Dev 010 from the font list and type Hkkjr. If you see भारत, the font is installed and working. Now type fganh: you should get हिंदी. Notice that the ि sign is typed before its letter in Kruti Dev - that is how the typewriter did it.
When it does not appear or does not work

• Not in the font list: Word was open during the install. Close all its windows, including any minimised to the taskbar, and reopen. Still missing? Open C:\Windows\Fonts and search for "Kruti". If nothing is there, the install never happened.
  • "Not a valid font file": the download is damaged, or it is not a font at all. Get the file again from another source.
  • Still English letters: the text is set in a font with another name - often a variant from the typist's computer. Select all, choose Kruti Dev 010 again, and compare.
  • A few letters wrong: you have another member of the family. Remove it from the Fonts folder and install 010.
On a Mac

Double-click the .ttf. Font Book opens with a preview. Press Install. If Font Book reports a problem with the file, it is usually a damaged download - the font itself installs normally on current macOS. Restart Word or Pages afterwards. Keynote and Pages treat Kruti Dev like any other font, but the text is still legacy text: a Mac without the font shows English letters, exactly as Windows does.
Removing a wrong or old version

Two fonts with the same name confuse Word, and a wrong member of the family stays in use until it is removed. Open C:\Windows\Fonts, type "Kruti" in the search box, and look at what is there. Right-click anything that is not Kruti Dev 010 and you no longer need, and choose Delete. Then install 010 again and restart Word. If Windows says the font is in use, close all your programs first, or restart the computer and delete it before opening anything.
Sending Kruti Dev files to others

The font is on your computer, not inside the file. Anyone you send a .docx to needs Kruti Dev 010 as well, or they will see English letters. If they only need to read it, send a PDF (File → Save As → PDF), which carries the letter shapes with it. If they need to edit it on a phone, in Google Docs or on a website, convert it to Unicode first with the Kruti Dev to Unicode converter.
Do you need to install it at all?

Only if you have to type or edit in Kruti Dev - for an exam, a court or a department template. To read or reuse Kruti Dev text, a converter is quicker than installing anything, and the Kruti Dev 010 font page has one at the top.

kruti-dev-text-shows-english-letters.h1: Why Kruti Dev Text Shows English Letters (and How to Fix It)
kruti-dev-text-shows-english-letters.title: Kruti Dev Text in English Letters? How to Fix
kruti-dev-text-shows-english-letters.description: Why a Hindi file typed in Kruti Dev turns into letters like Hkkjr and fgUnh, and three ways to fix it: install the font, re-apply it, or convert to Unicode.
kruti-dev-text-shows-english-letters.lede: You open a Hindi document and it reads Hkkjr ljdkj instead of भारत सरकार. Nothing is corrupted. The text was typed in Kruti Dev, and the computer showing it does not have that font.
body: What is really in the file

Kruti Dev is a legacy font. When a typist presses H, k, k, j, r, the file stores exactly those five English letters, and Kruti Dev 010 draws them as भारत. The Hindi was never in the file - it was in the font.
{{diagram:stored-vs-shown}}

So when the font is missing, or the text is set in another font, you see the stored letters. The same file opens correctly on the typist's computer and wrongly on yours, which makes it look as if something broke on the way. It did not.
Three ways to fix it
1. Install Kruti Dev 010

If you need to keep working in Kruti Dev - an office template, an exam, a court filing - install the font and reopen the file. The installation guide takes you through it. This is the only fix that leaves the file exactly as it is.
2. Put the font back on the text

Sometimes the font is installed but the text is not using it. That happens after pasting with "Keep Text Only", after changing a template, or when a file typed in a variant ("Kruti Dev 011", "Kruti Dev 010 Condensed") is opened where only 010 exists. Select the text and choose Kruti Dev 010.
3. Convert it to Unicode

If the text has to read correctly everywhere - on phones, in email, in Google Docs, on a website, in a search box - convert it to Unicode Hindi. Paste it into the Kruti Dev to Unicode converter, or upload the whole .docx. The result is real Devanagari that any Hindi font can show.
Which font is the text really in?
Before fixing anything, click inside the English-looking text and read the font box on Word's Home tab.

• It says Kruti Dev 010, but you still see English letters: the font is not installed on this computer. Install it, or convert.
  • It says Calibri, Arial or another English font: the text lost its font. Select it and choose Kruti Dev 010 (fix 2 above).
  • The box is empty when you select a paragraph: the paragraph mixes fonts. Select a single word at a time to find the Kruti Dev parts.

Excel and PowerPoint behave the same way: the font belongs to each cell or text box, so a sheet can show Hindi in one column and English letters in the next. Select the column and set Kruti Dev 010, or convert the cells.
Documents that mix English and Kruti Dev

Office letters often have English headings and Kruti Dev body text in the same file. The Word file converter on this site changes only the text set in Kruti Dev and leaves everything in English fonts alone, so a mixed document comes out right without any sorting by hand. See how to convert a whole Word file.
Recognising Kruti Dev

Once you know it, Kruti Dev is easy to spot: lots of k (the ा sign), f before consonants (the ि sign), and patterns like dk (का), gS (है) and vkSj (और). If you see boxes or question marks instead, that is a different problem - see why Hindi shows boxes or question marks. If it converts but many letters are wrong, the file may be in another legacy font such as Chanakya, which uses different keys. The list of converters shows what is supported.
Stopping it happening again

• Send a PDF when the other person only needs to read the document.
  • Keep a Unicode copy of anything that will be emailed, uploaded or published.
  • When a Kruti Dev file must go out, tell the recipient the font: "Kruti Dev 010".

kruti-dev-vs-unicode-government-work.title: Kruti Dev vs Unicode for Government Work
kruti-dev-vs-unicode-government-work.description: Kruti Dev or Unicode for official Hindi work? How they differ, where each is still required, and how to move between them without losing matras or conjuncts.
kruti-dev-vs-unicode-government-work.lede: Most offices now have both: old files and templates in Kruti Dev, new portals and e-Office in Unicode. Here is how they differ, where each still belongs, and how to switch without retyping.
body: The difference in one picture
Both look the same on screen and on paper. What differs is what the file stores.
{{diagram:storage-compare}}

Kruti Dev stores English key codes and relies on its font to draw them as Hindi. Unicode stores the Devanagari letters themselves, so any Hindi font - Mangal, Nirmala UI, Kokila, Noto Sans Devanagari - can show them, and any program can search, sort or spell-check them.
Side by side

• Opens correctly everywhere: Unicode does. Kruti Dev only where the font is installed.
  • Phones, WhatsApp, email, Google Docs: Unicode works, but Kruti Dev shows English letters.
  • Search: searching a Unicode file for भारत finds it. In a Kruti Dev file you would have to search for Hkkjr.
  • Websites, portals and e-Office: expect Unicode.
  • Many typing exams, courts and district offices: still use Kruti Dev on the Remington layout.
  • Printing: both print the same.
What official guidance says

For years the central government's Department of Official Language has encouraged offices to use Unicode for Hindi, and national systems such as NIC's e-Office expect Unicode text. In practice adoption is uneven: many state departments, courts and tehsil offices still work from Kruti Dev templates, and many recruitment typing tests still ask for it. If your department has issued an instruction, follow it. If not, the rule below works.
A practical rule

1. New documents: type in Unicode. They will open correctly for the next reader, and the one after that.
  2. Templates that must stay Kruti Dev: keep them in Kruti Dev, and keep a Unicode copy of anything that will be emailed or uploaded.
  3. Old records: convert them to Unicode when you next need them. A converted file can be searched, which matters more each year as archives grow.
  4. Exams: practise in whatever the notification names - often Kruti Dev on Remington, though some exams, such as CPCT, use Unicode with InScript or a Remington layout.
Common worries about switching

• "Our typists only know Remington." They can keep it. A Unicode Remington layout, or typing in Kruti Dev and converting, gives Unicode output from the same fingers. The Remington Hindi keyboard shows the idea: Remington keys in, Unicode out.
  • "Will printouts look different?" Only the typeface changes. Mangal and Nirmala UI look a little different from Kruti Dev 010, but the text is identical, and letters, orders and notices print as before.
  • "Our old files will stop working." They will not. Kruti Dev files keep opening wherever the font is installed. Convert them when you need them, not all at once.
Moving an office to Unicode: a checklist

1. List the templates that must stay Kruti Dev (a court format, an exam form) and leave those alone.
  2. Convert the rest as they come up, and file the Unicode copy next to the original.
  3. Check every converted document's names, figures and dates before it goes out.
  4. Set Mangal or Nirmala UI as the Hindi font in Word's Normal template so new files start in Unicode.
  5. Keep PDFs of anything that must look exactly as signed.
Moving between them without damage

Conversion is not a letter-for-letter swap. Kruti Dev types the ि sign before its consonant and the reph (र्) after its syllable. Unicode stores both the other way round. Split vowel signs and conjuncts such as क्ष, त्र and द्ध need care too. A careless converter produces text that looks nearly right and is wrong in exactly the words that matter: names and legal terms.

The converters on this site do this reordering and are tested on real documents: Kruti Dev to Unicode, Unicode to Kruti Dev and Kruti Dev to Mangal. They run in your browser, so draft orders and personal records are never uploaded.

convert-word-file-from-kruti-dev.h1: How to Convert a Whole Word File from Kruti Dev to Unicode
convert-word-file-from-kruti-dev.title: Convert a Kruti Dev Word File to Unicode
convert-word-file-from-kruti-dev.description: Convert a whole Kruti Dev .docx to Unicode Hindi in your browser, keeping tables, bold and layout - and what to do with .doc files and PDFs.
convert-word-file-from-kruti-dev.lede: Copying a long document into a converter page by page loses its tables and formatting and takes an afternoon. You can convert the whole .docx at once instead, with the layout intact and without uploading it anywhere.
body: What you need
A Word file in .docx format (or a plain .txt) typed in Kruti Dev, up to 20 MB. You do not need Kruti Dev installed, and nothing is uploaded: the file is opened and converted by your browser.
{{diagram:docx-flow}}
Step by step

1. Open Kruti Dev to Unicode and choose the Upload Word file tab above the text boxes.
  2. Drag your .docx onto the box, or press Choose file.
  3. Choose the Hindi font the converted file should use.
  4. Press Download converted file. You get a new .docx and your original is not changed.
The summary tells you how many paragraphs and tables were converted. If part of the file was already Unicode, it says so and leaves that part as it is.
What is kept and what changes

• Changes: text in Kruti Dev becomes Unicode Hindi, with the matras and reph put in Unicode order.
  • Kept: English text, numbers, tables, images, headers and footers, bold, italic, sizes, alignment and page layout.
  • Font: converted text gets the Unicode font you chose, so it shows correctly on any computer.
Old .doc files, PDFs and scans

• .doc (Word 97-2003): open it in Word and use File → Save As → Word Document (.docx), then convert the .docx. The same goes for password-protected files: remove the password first.
  • PDF: text copied from a PDF typed in Kruti Dev is usually still Kruti Dev keys, so it can be pasted into the converter - but PDFs often break lines and spacing. If you have the original .docx, use that instead.
  • Scanned pages: a scan is a picture, not text. It needs Hindi OCR first. A converter cannot read it.
Check before you rely on it

Read the converted file against the original, and give names, figures and dates special attention. Two things are worth knowing. English detection is a best guess - Kruti Dev stores Hindi as English letters, so an unusual English name can be converted by mistake. And a file typed in another font (Chanakya, or a Kruti Dev variant other than 010) will convert with some letters wrong, so check the font name in Word before you start.
A five-minute check of the result

1. Page count. The converted file should have about the same number of pages. A big difference usually means a font substitution, not lost text.
  2. First lines of each page. Read them against the original.
  3. Anything left unconverted. Kruti Dev text that was not converted still reads as English letters. Use Word's Find (Ctrl+F) for common Kruti Dev words such as dk, gS and vkSj: in a converted file they should not appear.
  4. Names, numbers and dates, one by one.
Converting many files

The converter takes one file at a time, and each takes a few seconds. For a folder of documents, keep the originals in one folder and save each converted copy into another with the same name, so nothing is overwritten and you can always go back. If a file is too large, split it into parts in Word and convert each part.
Going the other way

If an office template needs Kruti Dev, Unicode to Kruti Dev converts a Unicode .docx the same way and sets Kruti Dev 010 on every converted paragraph. And if you just need the text in Mangal, Kruti Dev to Mangal does the conversion for pasted text.

hindi-typing-speed-tips-for-exams.h1: Hindi Typing Speed Tips for Exams: A Four-Week Plan
hindi-typing-speed-tips-for-exams.title: Hindi Typing Speed Tips for SSC, CPCT
hindi-typing-speed-tips-for-exams.description: How to raise your Hindi typing speed for SSC, CPCT and court exams: accuracy first, the keys that cost the most time, a four-week plan and exam-day habits.
hindi-typing-speed-tips-for-exams.lede: Most candidates try to get faster by typing faster. It is the slowest way there. Speed in Hindi typing comes from accuracy, from the handful of keys that cost the most time, and from stamina - in that order.
body: 1. Get clean before you get quick

Type at whatever pace keeps you above 95% accurate, even if it feels absurdly slow. Every error costs you twice: the wrong keystroke, and the correction or the penalty. Exams score net speed, so a steady, clean 28 WPM beats a careless 35. Once accuracy holds for a week, the speed comes without being chased.
2. Stop looking at your hands

Each glance down costs your place in the passage and resets your rhythm. Keep the keyboard chart beside the screen, or use the on-screen keyboard in the typing tutor, which lights the next key and the finger that presses it.
3. Drill the keys that cost the most

In Kruti Dev, a small set of letters slows almost everyone down:

  • The ि sign, typed before its consonant (fd for कि). Unlearning the spoken order takes deliberate practice.
  • Two-key letters - भ, श, ष, ण, ध, ख, घ, झ, थ - each a half form plus the ा stroke.
  • The reph, typed after its syllable (deZ for कर्म).
  • Shift letters, held with the little finger of the other hand.

After every test, look at "Keys you missed most" on the result and spend ten minutes on those alone.
4. Build stamina at the exam length

A 10-minute test is a different skill from a 1-minute burst. Typists who are comfortable for one minute are often finished by minute eight. In the last weeks, sit at least one test a day at your exam's full length - the tests here run from 1 minute to 2 hours, and the clock can be paused if you are interrupted.
{{diagram:practice-plan}}
5. Little and often

Thirty minutes every day beats four hours on a Sunday. Muscle memory settles between sessions, not during them, so daily practice compounds in a way that weekend marathons do not. Log each result in the progress log. Seeing the line rise is what keeps most people going.
6. Rehearse exam conditions

• Use the same layout as the exam. Check the notification: Kruti Dev means Remington and Mangal usually means InScript.
  • Practise with and without correcting errors, since exams differ on backspace.
  • Sit on a chair and at a desk like the exam centre's, with feet flat, wrists level and the screen at eye height.
  • On the day, read the first line before starting the clock, then keep going: a missed word costs less than a stopped rhythm.
7. Set up your desk once

Speed depends on comfort more than people expect. Sit so your elbows are at the height of the keyboard and bent at a right angle, keep your wrists level rather than resting on the edge of the desk, and put the screen at eye height so you are not looking down all session. Rest your fingers lightly on the home row - a s d f and j k l ; - and let them return there after every key. Take a short break every 20-30 minutes of practice.
Myths that cost candidates time

• "Type fast from day one." Speed practised with errors turns the errors into habits.
  • "Only long passages matter." Short, focused drills on your weak keys raise speed faster, while long tests build stamina. You need both.
  • "The keyboard layout does not matter." It is the one thing you cannot change on the day. Learn the one your exam names.
  • "Hindi WPM is just English WPM." In Kruti Dev many letters take two or three keys, so the same WPM means fewer Hindi words. Judge your progress by net WPM on Hindi passages.
When you are ready, time yourself on the exam typing test, which explains how SSC, CPCT and court exams count speed.

remington-vs-inscript-keyboard.h1: Remington vs InScript: Which Hindi Keyboard Layout Should You Learn?
remington-vs-inscript-keyboard.title: Remington vs InScript Hindi Keyboard | Differences and Which to Learn
remington-vs-inscript-keyboard.description: Remington (Kruti Dev) and InScript (Unicode) put Hindi letters on different keys. How they differ, which exams and offices use each, and which one to learn.
remington-vs-inscript-keyboard.lede: Hindi has two main keyboard layouts, and practising the wrong one wastes months. Remington is the typewriter layout behind Kruti Dev. InScript is the standard layout built into Windows, Android and every Unicode system.
body: Where they came from

Remington is the layout of the Hindi typewriter. When offices moved to computers, fonts such as Kruti Dev 010 and DevLys kept the same keys, so typists did not have to relearn anything. InScript was designed later by the Government of India for computers. It arranges letters logically - vowels on the left, consonants on the right - and it types real Unicode Hindi, with any Hindi font.
{{diagram:home-row-compare}}
How they differ in practice

• Letter positions: most letters are on different keys. On InScript k is क, but on Remington it is the ा sign.
  • The ि sign: on Remington you type it before the consonant, as it is drawn. On InScript you type it after, as it is pronounced.
  • What you get: classic Remington with Kruti Dev produces legacy text that needs the font. InScript produces Unicode. Unicode versions of the Remington layout also exist, and some exams offer one.
  • Learning curve: InScript's logical grouping is easier for a beginner, but Remington is what typing institutes and older typists know.
Which exams and offices use which

Many court, district and state clerical typing tests still set Hindi typing in Kruti Dev on Remington. SSC and CPCT let candidates choose, and name the options in the notification. Central government offices, e-Office and anything online work in Unicode, where InScript is native. Your notification or your office manual is the final word, so read it before you start practising.
Which one should you learn?

• Preparing for an exam that names Kruti Dev or Remington: learn Remington. The typing tutor teaches it lesson by lesson.
  • Starting from scratch for office or everyday work: InScript is the better long-term choice, because it is built into every modern system and produces Unicode directly.
  • Already fast on Remington: stay with it. Type on the Remington Hindi keyboard page to get Unicode output, or convert your Kruti Dev text with Kruti Dev to Unicode.
Switching from one to the other

Expect a few weeks of slow typing. Fingers trained on one layout keep reaching for the old keys, especially under time pressure, and speed drops before it recovers. Three things help:

  • Switch completely. Using both layouts during the same weeks slows learning on each.
  • Start with the home row and build outwards, exactly as you did the first time - the tutor's lesson order works for relearning too.
  • Keep a chart beside the screen rather than looking at the keyboard, so the new positions go into memory instead of your eyes.
Remington that types Unicode

Some exam software and input tools offer a Unicode version of the Remington layout. CPCT, for example, lists a Remington option next to InScript. The main letters sit where a Kruti Dev typist expects them, but a few symbols and conjuncts can differ between versions, so check the exam's own key chart for the keys you use most. Practising on Kruti Dev still trains the right muscle memory for the letters themselves.
Trying both

To try InScript, add Hindi in Windows Settings → Time & language → Language & region and switch with Windows key + Space. To see the whole Remington layout, print the one-page Kruti Dev keyboard chart. And if you only need a few words of Hindi, neither layout is necessary: English to Hindi typing or the on-screen Hindi keyboard will do.

hindi-text-shows-boxes-or-question-marks.h1: Hindi Text Shows Boxes or Question Marks? How to Fix It
hindi-text-shows-boxes-or-question-marks.title: Hindi Showing Boxes or Question Marks?
hindi-text-shows-boxes-or-question-marks.description: Why Hindi text turns into empty boxes, question marks or odd symbols in Word, Excel, email and websites - and the fix for each case.
hindi-text-shows-boxes-or-question-marks.lede: Boxes, question marks and English letters look like one problem, but they are three different ones with three different fixes. Find the symptom you have below.
body: {{diagram:symptoms}}
Empty boxes: the font has no Hindi

Boxes (sometimes called "tofu") mean the text is fine - it is real Unicode Hindi - but the font on it has no Devanagari letters. Arial, Calibri and Times New Roman are common culprits. Select the text and choose a Hindi font: Mangal, Nirmala UI, Kokila or Aparajita on Windows, Noto Sans Devanagari anywhere. In Word, set it under Complex scripts in the Font dialog (Ctrl+D) to change a whole document at once.
On very old systems, such as Windows XP without Indic support, Hindi can show as boxes whatever the font. The fix there is to enable complex script support, or to use a newer device.
Question marks: the letters were lost

Question marks mean the Hindi was saved or sent through something that could not hold it - a text file saved in "ANSI" instead of UTF-8, an old database, or a form that strips non-English characters. The Hindi was replaced by ? at that point, and it cannot be recovered from the question marks. Go back to the source, and save or export it as UTF-8: in Notepad, File → Save As → Encoding: UTF-8. In Excel, choose CSV UTF-8.
Strange accented letters: the right bytes read the wrong way

Text like à¤­à¤¾à¤°à¤¤ is UTF-8 Hindi being read as a Western encoding. Nothing is lost. Open the file again and choose UTF-8: in Excel, use Data → From Text/CSV and pick 65001: Unicode (UTF-8). In a browser or email program, set the text encoding to UTF-8.
English letters: it is Kruti Dev

Letters like Hkkjr or fgUnh are not an encoding problem at all. The text was typed in the Kruti Dev font, which stores Hindi as English key codes, and the font is missing. Install Kruti Dev 010, or convert the text to Unicode with Kruti Dev to Unicode. Why Kruti Dev shows English letters explains it in full.
In Excel and CSV files

Double-clicking a CSV file makes Excel guess its encoding, and it often guesses wrong for Hindi, giving accented nonsense. Open Excel first, then use Data → From Text/CSV, choose 65001: Unicode (UTF-8) as the file origin, and load. When saving a sheet with Hindi as CSV, choose CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited), not plain CSV, or the Hindi will become question marks.
For website and form owners

If Hindi entered in your own website or form comes back as question marks, the page or the database is not using UTF-8. The page needs <meta charset="utf-8">, and a MySQL database needs the utf8mb4 character set on its tables and connection. Data already saved as question marks cannot be repaired. Fix the setting and collect it again.
On phones and in apps

Modern Android and iPhone devices show Unicode Hindi out of the box. If Hindi shows as boxes in one app only, that app is using its own font, so update it. If Kruti Dev text reaches a phone, it will always show as English letters, because phones cannot install Kruti Dev - send Unicode instead.
Preventing it

• Type new Hindi in Unicode, with a Unicode font, as described in how to type Hindi in MS Word.
  • Save text and CSV files as UTF-8.
  • Before a document goes out, open it on another computer or phone and check that the Hindi reads correctly.

kruti-dev-typing-rules-matras-reph-half-.h1: Kruti Dev Typing Rules: Matras, Reph, Half Letters and Conjuncts
kruti-dev-typing-rules-matras-reph-half-.title: Kruti Dev Typing Rules | How to Type ि, Reph, Half Letters & Conjuncts
kruti-dev-typing-rules-matras-reph-half-.description: The rules behind Kruti Dev typing: why ि comes first, where the reph goes, how half letters, rakar and conjuncts like क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ and श्र are typed.
kruti-dev-typing-rules-matras-reph-half-.lede: Kruti Dev follows the typewriter: you type what is drawn, left to right, not what is spoken. Five rules explain almost every sequence that trips people up.
body: {{diagram:typing-order}}
Rule 1: the ि sign comes first

The short-i sign is drawn on the left of its consonant, so on the typewriter it is typed first: f then the consonant. कि is fd, हिंदी is fganh. With a half letter the ि goes before the whole cluster, because it is drawn before all of it. Unicode stores the same sign after the consonant, which is why converting Kruti Dev is more than a letter swap.
Rule 2: the reph comes last

The reph - the small र् hook on top of a letter, as in कर्म or धर्म - is typed after the syllable it sits on, with Z: कर्म is deZ, धर्म is /keZ. If the syllable has a vowel sign, the reph still comes after it.
Rule 3: letters without a key are a half form plus ा

Several full letters have no key of their own. They are typed as their half form followed by k, the ा stroke: भ is Hk, ध is /k, श is 'k. On the typewriter the vertical stroke was the same piece of metal as the ा sign, and Kruti Dev keeps that.
Rule 4: half letters for conjuncts

To join two consonants, type the half form of the first and then the second: क्य is D;, and क्या is D;k. Many half forms are on Shift - D is क्, E is म् - and the rest are the letter without its ा stroke. Where a letter has no half form, such as ड or ट, use the halant key (~) after it.
Rule 5: rakar, and the conjuncts with their own keys

The small stroke of र under a consonant, as in प्र or क्र, is z, typed after the consonant: प्र is iz. Four common conjuncts are drawn as single shapes and have keys of their own or short sequences: क्ष ({k), त्र (=), ज्ञ (K) and श्र (J). Learn them as letters, not as combinations.
Signs worth learning early

• Nukta (the dot under ड़, ज़, फ़) is +, typed after the letter: ड़ is M+.
  • Anusvara (ं) is a, typed after the syllable: गंगा is xaxk.
  • Visarga (ः) is %: दुःख is nq%[k.
  • The full stop । is A (Shift + a).
  • Chandrabindu (ँ) has no key on a normal keyboard. Hold Alt and type 0161 on the number pad: चाँद is pk¡n.
Mistakes almost everyone makes

• Typing ि after the consonant, the way it is spoken. The sign then lands on the next letter.
  • Typing the reph before the syllable. In Kruti Dev it always comes last: कार्य is dk;Z.
  • Using the halant key where a half-letter key exists. D gives a proper half क्, while d~ gives क with a visible halant, which looks wrong in print.
  • Leaving Caps Lock on. Every capital is a different Hindi letter.
Why these rules matter when converting

Unicode stores Hindi in the order it is spoken: consonant, then vowel sign, and the reph as a र with a halant before its syllable. A Kruti Dev to Unicode converter has to move every ि and every reph to its Unicode position, and rebuild each two-key letter as one character. The converters on this site do exactly that, and the typing tutor uses the same rules to check your keystrokes - so what the tutor teaches and what the converters read are the same thing.
Practising them

The matra and conjunct chart lists twenty signs and conjuncts with their exact keys, and prints on one page. The typing tutor drills them in lessons 6 to 8. And the Remington Hindi keyboard lets you type any word and see its Unicode immediately.
